name: 築地寿司清 築地本店
cuisine: Edomae sushi counter in the Tsukiji outer market, open since 1889 — nigiri à la carte at ¥220–660 a piece, or sets at ¥1,850 (和) / ¥3,500 (匠) / ¥4,500 (おまかせ) / ¥6,000 (おまかせ極); the lunch 大名ちらし is ¥2,500. Reckon ¥2,500 at lunch, ¥4,000 at night.
neighborhood: Tsukiji 4-chōme, inside the outer market — 5 min from Tsukiji (Tokyo Metro Hibiya line), 3 min from Tsukijishijō (Toei Ōedo line)
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim and no allergen page anywhere on the company site. This is a straight Edomae counter: the nikiri brushed on the nigiri is ordinary wheat shōyu, the anago is finished with a soy-mirin tsume, and the tamagoyaki that goes on the counter in this market is made with soy sauce as a matter of course (the neighbouring specialist 大定, two doors along at 4-13-11, prints 「原材料の一部に小麦、大豆を含む」 on its own egg blocks). Nothing published shows a tamari line or any wheat-free handling. A celiac would be relying entirely on an unrehearsed conversation with the itamae.
vegan_detail: Nothing on the published menu is vegan. Nigiri, sashimi platters, shellfish, house shiokara, grilled squid legs, anago shirayaki, tuna-and-negi skewers — the only non-animal items are the drinks. No vegetable course exists.

roles: operated by 築地寿司清株式会社 (TSUKIJISUSHISAY CO., LTD.)
chef_bio.origin: Tsukiji, Chūō-ku — founded here in 明治22年 (1889)
chef_bio.background: Tsukiji Sushisei is one of the market's genuine old houses: the company's own site dates the founding to 明治22年 (1889) and describes 130-odd years of Edomae technique, now buying from Toyosu since the inner market moved. From that one counter it has become a department-store sushi group of roughly thirty branches — Ginza, Hibiya Chanter, Tokyo Station Gransta, Isetan Shinjuku, Mitsukoshi Nihonbashi, and on to Kyoto, Osaka, Nagoya, Niigata and Hakata — but the 築地本店 at 4-13-9 remains the flagship, with a 16-seat counter downstairs, a 10-seat counter and 8 table seats upstairs. The house style is deliberately unintimidating for a shop of its age: pieces are individually priced from ¥220, the room is entirely non-smoking, and cards, IC cards and phone payment are all taken. No individual chef is named publicly; the company presents the kitchen collectively as 板前の確かな技.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「本物の江戸前寿司」をより多くの方に気軽に — real Edomae sushi at a price an ordinary person can walk in and pay.
chef_bio.specialty: おまかせ-極- ¥6,000 (counter only); the ¥2,500 大名ちらし at lunch; anago shirayaki ¥1,800; house-made shiokara ¥600.

anecdotes.text: The shop lists its own founding as 明治22年 (1889) and now sources from Toyosu rather than the old Tsukiji inner market — the site's phrasing is 「豊洲市場の厳選した素材で、130余年の歴史で培ってきた『本物の江戸前寿司』」.
There are two Sushisei counters a few metres apart in the market — 築地本店 and 築地新館 — and the company's news page has had to tell customers when one closes for building work and the other stays open.
It is one of the eateries listed by the Tsukiji outer-market association itself in the 寿司 category of its official shop directory.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The company site's 築地本店 page carries the full priced menu, the address 〒104-0045 東京都中央区築地4-13-9, phone 03-3541-7720, the weekday/weekend hours, the Wednesday closure, the seat counts and the payment methods, and was read directly. The outer-market association's own 寿司 category listing includes 築地寿司清 本店 and confirms it as a market member. Tabelog's listing agrees on address, phone and a 10:00 opening.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A sushi counter, so no flour or noodle line — but no wheat-free protocol is claimed either, and the same hands and cloths work every piece.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard wheat shōyu assumed throughout; no gluten-free tamari is named anywhere on the site, and the anago is served with a soy-and-mirin tsume.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Whole menu is fish and shellfish; there is no vegetable set and no dashi disclosure.

positives.text: Per-piece pricing from ¥220 means you can order round the things you cannot eat rather than commit to a fixed course; the counter is entirely non-smoking and takes cards.

cultural_comfort.note: One of the least intimidating old sushi counters in Tokyo. It opens at 10:00, so you can eat sushi at a civilised hour without the pre-dawn market queue; walk-ins are the norm and reservations are only taken from 17:00. Prices are printed per piece, all seats are non-smoking, and credit cards, IC cards and phone payment are accepted, which is not a given in this market. Closed Wednesdays — the day the market itself is shut — so check the market calendar before you go. Dietary requests would need to be made in Japanese at the counter.

enrich_note: Confirmed. The light record's 「築地寿司清」 is the real 築地寿司清 築地本店 at 中央区築地4-13-9; name extended to the branch name. Address, hours, menu and prices read off the company's own store page (the site is HTTP-only and its TLS certificate does not match, so it must be fetched over http); the outer-market association lists the shop in its official 寿司 directory. Coordinates are the GSI Japan geocode of 築地4-13-9, about 600 m from the neighbourhood-centroid pin the light record carried.

name: 大定 場外本店
cuisine: Tamagoyaki specialist trading since 1924 — hand-rolled Edo-style egg blocks sold whole over the counter, from ¥680 for the standard つきじ野 (about 560 g) to ¥1,400 for the darker, coarser 江戸前 (about 650 g); takeaway only, no seats.
neighborhood: Tsukiji 4-chōme, in the outer market — about 4 min from Tsukiji (Tokyo Metro Hibiya line, exit 1) and 4 min from Tsukijishijō (Toei Ōedo line)
hours_raw: 6:00～15:00（公式サイトの営業時間変更告知）。他掲載では 4:00～14:30（土曜は15:00まで）。日曜・祝日・市場休市日は休業。
gf_detail: Ruled out on the shop's own labelling, not on inference. Daisada printed a full ingredient list for each product, and every one ends 「原材料の一部に小麦、大豆を含む」 — contains wheat and soy. The standard つきじ野 is 「鶏卵、上白糖、薄口醤油、塩、クエン酸、調味料（アミノ酸等）」 and the 江戸前 is 「鶏卵、上白糖、本膳醤油、塩、調味料（アミノ酸等）」, the shop naming ヒゲタの本膳醤油 as the soy it uses. Wheat soy sauce is in the batter itself, so there is no version of this that a celiac can eat.
vegan_detail: The product is egg. 鶏卵 is the first ingredient of every item; the shop specifies 地養卵 from Chiba. Nothing here is vegan or could be made so.

roles: 有限会社 大定 (Daisada Ltd.), family firm
chef_bio.origin: Tsukiji, Chūō-ku — trading in the Tokyo Central Wholesale Market since 大正13年 (1924)
chef_bio.background: Daisada is one of the handful of tamagoyaki houses that made Tsukiji's reputation for the thing, and it is a wholesaler first: its own copy says it has traded in the 東京築地中央卸売市場 for close to a century and supplies sushi restaurants, ryōriya and supermarkets across the country, with the retail counter at 築地4-13-11 as the shop-front of that business. Everything is 手焼き — rolled one block at a time by hand — and the house is specific about materials in a way most market shops are not: 地養卵 eggs, ヒゲタの本膳醤油, sea salt from Akō, and Hokkaidō alkaline water. The two anchors of the range are 「つきじ野」, the pale, gently sweet block aimed at high-end sushi counters, and 「江戸前」, a revival of the recipe the firm made in its founding years for the Imperial Household Agency and high-class caterers — the egg is whisked less, so white and yolk stay in visible contrast and the scorch marks and layers stand out. There is a seasonal line on top of that (涼梅 and 枝豆 in summer, 松茸焼 and 紅葉 in autumn, 伊達巻 in limited numbers for New Year) and an eight-piece sampler box. A second counter trades inside Toyosu market's 魚がし横丁. No individual chef is named; it is run as 有限会社 大定.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「信頼の味」 — a wholesaler's reliability, one block at a time, hand-rolled.
chef_bio.specialty: つきじ野 ¥680 (the standard, for sushi counters); 江戸前 ¥1,400 (the founding-era recipe); 江戸だし焼; 伊達巻 at New Year; seasonal 涼梅, 枝豆, 松茸焼, 紅葉.

anecdotes.text: The 江戸前 block is sold as a revival of the recipe Daisada made in its earliest years, when it was a designated supplier to the 宮内庁 and to high-class caterers — whisked less than a modern tamagoyaki so the white and yolk stay in contrast.
The shop's own customer quotes are market people: 「甘いの苦手なんだよね。こういう玉子焼が関東にあってうれしい。」 from a man who works for a seafood company.
Daisada's website announced a change of opening hours at the Tsukiji main shop to 6:00–15:00; older listings still print the market-trader hours of 4:00 onward.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: daisada.jp no longer resolves to the shop — the domain now serves a Plesk default page — so the company's own text was read from the Internet Archive's 2019-12-16 capture, which carries the founding year 大正13年, the 手焼き method, the named ingredients and the hours change, and from the archived product pages, which carry the full 原材料 lists including the wheat declaration. Chūō-ku's official tourism guide and Tokyo tamagoyaki write-ups independently give the address 東京都中央区築地4-13-11 and the phone 03-3541-6964.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Moot — the wheat is an ingredient, not a contaminant. Every product line declares 「原材料の一部に小麦、大豆を含む」.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Named explicitly: 薄口醤油 in つきじ野, and ヒゲタの本膳醤油 in 江戸前. Both are wheat-brewed shōyu, and both go into the egg mixture before it is rolled.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The product is egg. Not applicable.

staff_allergy_handling.text: A per-product 原材料 list was published for every item, which is more disclosure than most market stalls give — the wheat declaration is unambiguous rather than something you have to ask about.

cultural_comfort.note: A takeaway counter, not a restaurant: you point, you pay, you carry a block of tamagoyaki away — no Japanese needed and no seat to negotiate. The catch is the clock. It is a market shop that opens before dawn and shuts in the early afternoon, and it closes on Sundays, public holidays and every 市場休市日, so check the Tsukiji market calendar rather than turning up on a whim. Assume cash. Blocks keep five days refrigerated, which makes this a good thing to buy for a hotel-room breakfast; there is a second Daisada counter inside Toyosu market's Uogashi Yokochō if you are over there instead.

enrich_note: Confirmed, with the light record's cuisine label corrected. 「大定」 is real and is at 中央区築地4-13-11, but it is a 玉子焼 (tamagoyaki) specialist, not the 天ぷら the sweep recorded — the labels in this shard look shifted by one row, since the record above it carries 玉子焼き専門 against a kaisen-don shop. Name extended to 大定 場外本店 to distinguish it from the firm's Toyosu counter. The shop's own domain daisada.jp has lapsed and now serves a Plesk default page, so `website` is deliberately left off and the company's own text — founding year, method, hours change and the per-product 原材料 lists — was read from the Internet Archive's 2019-12-16 capture instead. Coordinates are the GSI Japan geocode of 築地4-13-11.

name: 岸田屋
cuisine: The Tsukishima drinking house people queue for — a 19-seat コの字 counter built around one pot of 牛にこみ, beef offal simmered soft under a heap of raw negi (¥950 as of June 2026), with nikudōfu, potato salad, nuta and simmered anago alongside; about ¥2,000–4,000 a head, cash only, no reservations.
neighborhood: Tsukishima 3-chōme — 4 min from Tsukishima station (Toei Ōedo line), 7 min from Tsukishima (Tokyo Metro Yūrakuchō line), 6 min from Kachidoki. This is NOT Tsukiji: it is across the Sumida on Tsukishima island, about 1.3 km east of the pin the light record carried.
hours_raw: 火・水・木・金・土 16:00～21:00　定休日：月曜日、日曜日、祝日
gf_detail: No gluten-free provision and none plausible here. The house dish is 煮込み simmered for hours in miso and soy — wheat shōyu by default — and the nikudōfu, the simmered anago and the nuta dressing come off the same seasoning shelf. There is no website, no allergen sheet and no English menu, and the room is nineteen counter seats working a five-hour service with a queue outside; this is not a kitchen that can stop and build a wheat-free plate. Nothing published claims a tamari or any wheat-free handling.
vegan_detail: A beef-offal house. The signature stew, the nikudōfu, the anago and the shirasu are all animal; the potato salad carries mayonnaise and the nuta is a vinegared-miso dressing normally built over fish or shellfish. Tabelog lists no vegetable course, and there is nothing on the board a vegan could eat.

roles: family-run taishū-sakaba; no chef or proprietor named publicly
chef_bio.background: Kishidaya is the reason people who are not chasing monjayaki still get off at Tsukishima. Tabelog's shop record gives an opening date of 1900 and notes that it started life as an お汁粉 shop — a sweet red-bean soup counter — and only became the izakaya it is now in 1966. What it became is one of the most admired drinking houses in Tokyo: selected for Tabelog's 居酒屋 百名店 EAST in 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025, scoring 3.71 across more than 1,400 reviews. The room is nineteen seats around a コの字 counter, no tables, no private space, no bookings taken, all of it non-smoking, and cash only — no cards, no e-money, no QR payment. The door opens at 16:00 and reviewers describe timing their arrival to make the first sitting; it closes Sundays, Mondays and public holidays. The board is short and the star is 牛にこみ, offal simmered until it gives way, buried under raw spring onion — the running line among regulars is that the negi is not a garnish but a requirement. No individual proprietor is put forward publicly: the identity of the place is the counter and the pot.
chef_bio.philosophy: Taishū-sakaba in the old sense — one famous dish, a short board, cash in hand, and no concessions to convenience.
chef_bio.specialty: 牛にこみ ¥950 (June 2026) — the beef-offal stew under a mound of negi; also 肉豆腐, ぬた, 穴子煮付, ポテトサラダ.

anecdotes.text: Tabelog's shop data records the business as opening in 1900 as an お汁粉 (sweet bean soup) shop and converting to the present izakaya in 1966 — 「1900年にお汁粉の店として創業、1966年に現在の居酒屋に」.
Selected for Tabelog's 居酒屋 百名店 EAST in 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025 — a top-hundred izakaya in eastern Japan four times over.
Because it takes no reservations, getting in means queueing: a July 2026 reviewer writes that it is not an enormous line, but you have to aim early if you want the first sitting.

A June 2026 visitor describes ducking under a noren that visibly shows its age into a loud コの字 counter, ordering a cold Kirin bottle and then, inevitably, the nikomi — the offal astonishingly soft under a pile of negi.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Kishidaya has no website. Its Tabelog shop page was opened directly and supplies the address 東京都中央区月島3-15-12, phone 03-3531-1974, 予約不可, the Tue–Sat 16:00–21:00 hours with Monday/Sunday/holiday closure, the ¥3,000–3,999 headline budget against a ¥2,000–2,999 figure from actual reviewer spend, 19 counter-only seats, 全席禁煙, カード不可・電子マネー不可・QRコード決済不可, the four 百名店 selections, the 1900 opening as an お汁粉 shop and 1966 conversion, and the current 牛にこみ price of ¥950. Reviews dated June and July 2026 confirm it is trading normally.

gf_cross_contamination.text: No allergen information exists in any form, and there is no room to ask: nineteen seats, one pot, a five-hour service and a queue on the pavement.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard wheat shōyu and miso assumed throughout — the signature dish is a long-simmered miso-and-soy nikomi and the anago, nikudōfu and nuta are seasoned from the same shelf. No tamari is claimed anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Beef offal is the house speciality and the stockpot is the centre of the kitchen; Tabelog lists no vegetable-only preparation on the board.

positives.text: All nineteen seats are non-smoking, which is not typical of a sakaba of this vintage.

cultural_comfort.note: The hard end of Tokyo drinking, and gloriously so. No reservations, no website, no English menu, nineteen seats on one コの字 counter, and a queue before the 16:00 opening — aim for the first sitting or expect to wait. Payment is cash only: no cards, no IC, no QR. The board is handwritten in Japanese and service moves fast, so ordering is expected to be quick and in Japanese, and a dietary negotiation would not land. Closed Sundays, Mondays and public holidays. Worth the trouble if you want the real article, but if you are travelling with a restriction this is not the place to test it — and note it is on Tsukishima, one Ōedo-line stop past the market district, not in Tsukiji at all.

enrich_note: Confirmed, but the light record put it in the wrong place and gave it the wrong food. 「岸田屋」 is real: a taishū-sakaba at 中央区月島3-15-12, 4 min from Tsukishima station on the Ōedo line, trading Tue–Sat 16:00–21:00 and reviewed as recently as July 2026. It is not in Tsukiji — it is about 1.3 km east across the Sumida — and it is not 海産物/新鮮魚介 but a beef-offal stew house. Its Tabelog page dates the business to 1900 (as an お汁粉 shop, izakaya from 1966), which contradicts the 明治10年/1877 founding that some review write-ups repeat; the shop record is used here. Coordinates moved to the GSI Japan geocode of 月島3-15-12. Nothing called 岸田屋 appears anywhere in the Tsukiji outer-market association's own eating-and-drinking directory, which was scraped in full (寿司 / 海鮮丼 / お食事 / 喫茶・軽食・居酒屋 / 玉子焼 / 魚河岸飲食 — 105 shops), so there is no second Tsukiji business of that name that this could be instead.
